discussion_comments.comment_body: Valid, fixed. A link whose target is a directory already on the current copy chain, or an ancestor of one (`.`, `..`, a sibling that links back), is now skipped and listed in `skippedPaths` instead of being expanded again, and the number of linked-directory expansions is capped (`MAX_LINK_EXPANSIONS`). Covered by "skips links that loop back into a directory being copied": twenty links to `.` plus one to `..` finish in well under a second with only the real content copied.

The header comment says provider-request building can middle-cut these outputs again in `session/services/message-builder.ts`. `truncateMiddleByChars` there (around line 1608) still uses `text.slice(0, keep)` and `text.slice(-keep)`, and `truncateToolResultContent` sends tool output through it. So once a long result hits that budget, the request can still carry a lone surrogate. Would it make sense to switch those two slices to `sliceUtf16` here too, or is that meant for a follow-up?

Good catch, thanks. `DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS` is 8,000, below the 48,000 command cap, so command output longer than that went through `truncateMiddleByChars` again on every request and could still pick up a lone surrogate. I've added it to this PR in ef1dbdf: both slices now use `sliceUtf16`, and that also covers the `truncateMiddleToBytes` byte backstop, since it calls the same function.

The new regression tests failed against the previous head before the fix (4 failed / 8 passed). They hit the tool-result cap at 101 and 102 chars and the aggregate byte budget at 9003 and 9004 bytes. After the fix, message-builder and output-limits pass 71/71 and the core `src/session` suite passes 180/180. I've updated the PR description, and message-builder is no longer in the follow-up list.

Also tightened the helper in `2393429ae` so only meaningful substrings participate in the partial-line diagnostic; very short SEARCH lines now stay on the generic no-match path, with regression coverage for both cases.
